::: {.public-hero}
## Why Some Young Pollock Make It

Most pollock eggs do not become adults. A strong year class happens when enough young fish pass through several survival gates and are still alive at age 3.
:::

::: {.big-message}
::: {.message-piece .many}
**Many**

eggs and larvae
:::

::: {.message-arrow}
-> 
:::

::: {.message-piece .few}
**Few**

age-3 recruits
:::

::: {.message-caption}
Recruitment is a filtering process, not a single event.
:::
:::

## The Survival Story

:::: {.public-story}
::: {.story-node .spawn}
[1]{.step-num} **Adults Spawn**

More adults can mean more eggs, but egg numbers are only the start.
:::

::: {.story-node .drift}
[2]{.step-num} **Young Fish Drift**

Winds, currents, temperature, and sea ice influence where eggs and larvae go.
:::

::: {.story-node .food}
[3]{.step-num} **Food Builds The Fuel Tank**

Tiny pollock need high-energy prey to grow and store enough reserves.
:::

::: {.story-node .winter}
[4]{.step-num} **Winter Tests The Fuel Tank**

Fish entering winter with more size and energy have a better chance.
:::

::: {.story-node .predators}
[5]{.step-num} **Predators Filter Survivors**

After the first winter, survival depends partly on whether young fish overlap with larger predators.
:::

::: {.story-node .recruits}
[6]{.step-num} **Age-3 Recruits**

The survivors become large enough to show up clearly in the assessment.
:::
::::

## Two Main Bottlenecks

::: {.bottleneck-card .food-gate}
### Food And Energy Gate

Young pollock need a full enough "fuel tank" before winter.

[]{.fuel-meter .high}

**Helps survival:** lipid-rich prey, good fall condition, enough summer production.

**Hurts survival:** poor prey match, low energy stores, warm metabolic demand without enough food.
:::

::: {.bottleneck-card .pred-gate}
### Predator Overlap Gate

Young pollock survive better when they avoid heavy overlap with predators.

[]{.overlap-meter}

**Helps survival:** separation from adult pollock, arrowtooth flounder, and other predators.

**Hurts survival:** warm or shifting conditions that place young fish and predators in the same area.
:::

## What Changes From Year To Year

::: {.driver-card .ice}
### Sea Ice

Changes bloom timing, prey production, and the cold pool.
:::

::: {.driver-card .wind}
### Wind And Mixing

Can deliver nutrients that support summer food production.
:::

::: {.driver-card .temp}
### Temperature

Affects development, metabolism, spawning location, and predator habitat.
:::

::: {.driver-card .space}
### Location

The same number of young fish can have different outcomes depending on where they drift and settle.
:::

## What We Know And What Would Help

::: {.knowledge-card .available}
### Data We Already Use

- adult pollock abundance,
- egg and larval surveys,
- sea ice, temperature, wind, and cold-pool indicators,
- zooplankton and diet observations,
- age-0 fish size and energy in sampled years,
- predator abundance and spatial overlap,
- age-3 recruitment from the assessment.
:::

::: {.knowledge-card .needed}
### Data That Would Help Most

- an annual fall age-0 energy index,
- better winter survival information,
- annual maps for age-1 and age-2 fish,
- predator diet and size-selective mortality by year,
- a cohort table that follows each year class from eggs to age 3.
:::

## Plain-Language Takeaway

::: {.takeaway-band}
Strong recruitment is not caused by one simple switch. It is most likely when young pollock are delivered to the right places, find enough high-energy food before winter, and avoid intense predator overlap after the first winter [@heintz2013; @mueter2006; @petrik2015; @spencer2016].
:::
